notes:
Summary: Verdigris Serveware is a middleware provider for ultra-low-latency trade signal delivery. Evaluating Redwood for inference serving of reranking and chat assistants during market hours. High sensitivity to p95/p99 tail latency and per-token cost. Interested in Redwood Optimize (batching/caching/quantization) and benchmark support.

Recent timeline & activities:
- 2025-11-15: inbound demo request via growth form; AE assigned (Maya Chen).
- 2025-12-02: intro call (ff-2025-12-02-1) — discussed workload characteristics and compliance needs.
- 2026-01-18: technical deep-dive with infra + ML (linked Fireflies ff-2026-01-18-verdigris-demo). Asked for perf baseline tests.
- 2026-01-25: sent security questionnaire (Drive: security-faq link); IT flagged KMS and data residency.
- 2026-02-09: architecture review with platform team — network egress questions remain.

Use-case & requirements (customer language / shorthand):
- Workload: reranking for trade alerts + customer-facing real-time chat for traders.
- Latency targets: p50 chat <50ms, p95 reranking <120ms at sustained 200-350 QPS; market-open spikes to 1k QPS tolerated with graceful degradation.
- Throughput: baseline 200-350 qps for rerank path; bursts to 1k qps for short windows.
- Cost sensitivity: aiming for <$0.15 per 1k tokens equivalent on typical rerank workloads; prefer recommendations to trade-off quantization vs. quality.
- Model preferences: open LLMs (Llama-family variants), smaller reranker ensembles; willingness to try 8-bit and 4-bit quantized variants if quality holds.
- Routing/fallback: want auto-fallback to smaller quantized model + regional routing to EU/NA with consistent API.
- Security: SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration (HSM), ability to pin models and retention controls for PII.

POC ask / benchmarking requests (explicit):
- Provide a perf matrix: models (fp16, 8-bit, 4-bit) x batch sizes x KV cache enabled/disabled; include p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens.
- End-to-end latency measured in our staging env (simulate market-open bursts).
- Hit-rate/caching guidance: prefix/KV cache sizing and expected hit improvements for our traffic.
- Suggested batching configs that keep tail latency within SLO while reducing cost.
- Quantization trade-off report: expected latency/cost delta and quality delta measured on our rerank eval set.

Quotes / notes from users:
- "We need predictable tail latency during market open — missing that costs us revenue." — Head of Platform
- SE note: "Prefer dedicated GPUs for baseline; want to test private/VPC later for data residency."

- Exact networking (VPC peering vs. private link) and egress budgeting.
- Final sign-off from finance on ARR range.
- Need Redwood to run bench in our staging cluster or provide reproducible harness.
